subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressures & next steps (FinBot)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@finbot.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressures & next steps (FinBot)

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our 30-minute discovery so we're all aligned and to capture the immediate next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- Rapid growth in usage has made per-inference cost the top blocker for new product experiments (embedding + chat flows).
- Current unit economics aren't sustainable for smaller LTV customers — backend costs spike with long-context prompts.
- Occasional latency spikes during peak periods causing timeouts in the product.

Current stack (what we heard):
- Model hosting: self-hosted on AWS (mix of EC2 GPU instances via SageMaker + Triton for serving).
- Models: using a mix of open LLMs (some quantized on-host) and a commercial checkpoint for larger-context routing.
- Telemetry: request logs + some token-level cost metrics exported to internal S3.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- 2–3x reduction in per-unit inference cost (token or request basis) for the high-volume use case.
- Tail latency under ~200ms for single-turn completions (95th percentile) for the chat UX.
- Maintain >=95% of current qualitative output quality for customer-facing prompts.

Openness to technical levers:
- Quantization: you said FinBot is open to 4-bit/8-bit quantization if it doesn't regress quality for critical prompts.
- Batching & caching: you currently do minimal batching; prefix caching is not widely implemented across services.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with Ben (solutions engineering) to review request logs and batching patterns — goal: identify quick wins for prefix caching and batching windows. (Proposed: Tue 2026-11-09, 10:00 PT)
2) Share a small sample of anonymized inference logs (token counts, latencies, node types) so our perf team can model expected cost reductions. You mentioned you can provide a 48-72 hour sample.
3) Run a 2-week pilot on Redwood Dedicated (we’ll size a reserved pool and run a controlled workload) — scope to be defined after the deep-dive.

Attachments: I attached a mutual action plan template (FinBot-MAP-20261105.xlsx) to capture owners and deadlines. I also added a placeholder for the log sample.

If that looks right, I’ll get Ben to schedule the deep-dive and I’ll prepare the pilot outline.

Thanks again — excited to see if we can materially improve your unit economics for the product.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

(O) 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressures & next steps (FinBot)

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures everything. A few clarifications / notes: 

- We can share a 72-hour anonymized sample by EOD Friday (will scrub user ids & payloads).
- On quantization: our ML team is comfortable trying 8-bit across the mid-sized LLMs; for the largest checkpoint we prefer testing 4-bit in a canary.
- Batching: most of our API traffic is single-request interactive chat, but we do have batch jobs for re-ranking/embeddings at night. If caching can reduce repeated prefix work for chat, that’s ideal.

Schedule Ben’s deep-dive and we’ll lock a time. Lauren (cc’d) will own coordinating the log export.

Jordan
CTO | FinBot
